summary: The worktree tool names a phase's branch the same way in every verb (BUG-11, a regression the phase-entry change had introduced under a branch template with initials), and --apply parses only under sweep. Doctor accepts the done verb's own close row as the completion record, matched on completedAt, and keeps its FINDING for a hand edit - it had been accusing every task closed in a linked worktree. The stored status of a phase and a linked bug is now the derived one: signoff, close-phase's merge stamp and done on a fix task store it, settle materialises it for an existing plan, the validator warns where the two disagree, and audit-lookup reads the derivation. Reviewed in phase mode: storing done latched where an input changed afterwards (a hand re-open, a commit repair), which the reopen verb and the repair's fixedIn clearing close, and the stub mirror could raise out of a landed merge, which it no longer can. Phase gate green with the tree unchanged; the invariant check found no breach.

tasks.title: Every manage-worktrees verb names a phase's branch the way add does, and --apply exists only where it means something
tasks.description: BUG-11. add names the branch through _branch.phase_answer(meta, phase, git user name); list, remove, sweep and parents_of compose it through wanted_branches(manifest)/parents_of(manifest) with no user name, so under a template with initials the worktree add just cut is listed as a stranger and remove says no worktree holds the phase's branch. One branch_of used by every verb. Also: one argparse parser lists --apply unscoped and add --apply is silently accepted while the usage scopes it to sweep - subparsers, or refuse it elsewhere. worktree.md: a new worktree has no installed dependencies; install inside it (a symlinked node_modules resolves into the main checkout and trips Vite's server.fs.allow).

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_manage_worktrees.py: repro that FAILS on current code - under a meta.branch template with the user's initials, add then list shows the new worktree as a stranger and remove finds nothing

tasks.title: Doctor accepts the verb's task.done row as the completion record and keeps the FINDING for a done task with none
tasks.description: Measured on this repo: doctor prints a FINDING naming ten tasks closed by audit-task.py done in worktree phases. journal-writes derives task.complete only for a task it saw open in its before-snapshot, and it resolves the session's project dir, so a task closed in a linked worktree, or added and closed in one Bash call, gets none. audit-task.py's _journal_done writes task.done and says that row is the record of the close where no hook watches; _doctor_completions reads task.complete alone. Accept a task.done row whose completedAt matches the task's as the receipt; keep the FINDING (and its tier) for a done task with neither - the allow case that must stay red is a hand-flipped status.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__doctor_completions.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a done task whose journal holds task.add and task.done (via cli) but no task.complete is reported as edited outside the pipeline

outcome.technical: has_receipt accepts a task.done row whose completedAt equals the task's; the era starts at the first receipt of either kind.
outcome.descriptive: Doctor no longer accuses tasks closed by the done verb of being edited outside the pipeline; a hand-flipped task is still reported.

tasks.title: The stored status of a phase and a linked bug is the derived one: the verbs write it, lookup and the validator read the derivation
tasks.description: Since derived status, the signoff verb writes review.status and never status, so every signed-off phase keeps a stale stored status on its index stub and shard (this repo: in_progress on 24 signed-off phases, pending on 10), and a linked bug keeps triaged/in_progress with fixedIn null after its task is done. Raw readers - an older plugin's hooks (the installed 3.0.1 gate reads these phases as running), jq, an agent, a teammate - get the wrong answer. Decided: materialise. Every write that changes an input of effective_phase_status / effective_bug_status stores the derived value (signoff for a parent-branch phase, close-phase's mergedAt stamp for a branch phase, done for a bug's fix task; status and fixedIn), mirrored onto the stub. audit-lookup prints the derived value, and 'stored X, derived Y (basis ...)' where they differ. validate-manifest warns (additively) when stored and derived disagree, naming one command that settles an existing plan (a settle verb that materialises every derived value under the index lock, revalidated). orchestrator.md's status-mirror sentence and phase-signoff.md say what writes it. COMPATIBILITY: no reader may treat a stored done as authoritative over the derivation - check before changing.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: repro that FAILS on current code - after signoff (parent-branch phase) the stored status on the stub and the shard still reads in_progress while effective_phase_status says done

outcome.technical: signoff, close-phase's merge stamp and done on a fix task store the derived status (and fixedIn); settle materialises every derived value; validate warns on disagreement; audit-lookup reads the derivation.
outcome.descriptive: What the plan file says about a finished phase or a fixed bug is now true for any reader, and one command settles a plan that already carries stale values.

tasks.title: Sign-off review findings: a stored done survives re-open and repair, the stub mirror fails closed, settle is tested on both layouts, and the stale-status warning stays short
tasks.description:
Findings of the phase review, every one to be fixed (or answered with a measured reason) in this task:
R1 (med) plugins/audit/commands/run.md:21-25 (not in the diff) against plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py _locked_signoff/_settle and plugins/audit/scripts/git/close-phase.py:576-580 _store_derived: Storing `done` changes what the documented re-open path leads to. The derivation lets a stored terminal status win (_manifest_io.py:646-648), so once `done` is stored, later changes to the inputs no longer move it. run.md step 1's re-open resets the task to `pending` and reopens the linked bug, but leaves the phase alone. The phase keeps its stored `done` with an open task, and _manifest_phases.py:571-584 reports that as a FINDING ("status 'done' but N task(s) are not finished"). After that, every verb that validates before writing (settle does, at _locked_settle; start/done are the same kind of write) refuses with 'already invalid', so the re-opened task can no longer be closed through the verb. Before P69.3 the stored in_progress let the derivation follow the reopen. CHANGELOG's 'no reader's answer changes' and COMPATIBILITY's 'no write moves a value away' are true when the value is written, not afterwards. -> Change run.md step 1 so that re-open refuses a task whose phase's effective status is `done`, and points to a new task or /audit:bug instead. The alternative is for re-open to also reset the phase's stored status, but review.status stays recorded and signoff refuses a second sign-off, so that phase could never be signed again. Add a case that re-opens a task in a signed-off parent-branch phase and asserts the answer.
R2 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_commit_trail.py:324 (repair-commits.py --apply) against plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_manifest_io.py derived_disagreements (fixedIn arm) and plugins/audit/scripts/report/_report_html.py:238-240: `done` now stores bug.fixedIn = task.commit. repair-commits sets an unreachable task.commit to null but never touches bug.fixedIn. derived_disagreements only ever fills fixedIn and never replaces it, so no warning appears either. _bug_view prints the recorded fixedIn ahead of the task's commit, so after a history rewrite the bug keeps naming the dead SHA. Before this change, fixedIn was normally empty and would have read '—'. Changing task.commit changes an input of the derived fixedIn, and it is the one path left that leaves the stored copy behind with nothing reporting it. -> Two options: (a) repair-commits clears (and journals) a bug.fixedIn equal to a commit it clears; or (b) derived_disagreements reports a fixedIn that differs from its done fix task's commit when the stored value is the plugin's own copy. Add a case where repair-commits clears the fix task's commit and asserts the bug's fixedIn.
R3 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/git/close-phase.py:590-627 (mirror_stub) and 657-671 (stamp_merged): (a) `_panel_write.acquire_index_lock(...)` and `_panel_write.read_config(...)` are called before the try block. acquire only catches around `_locks.acquire`, so an exception from `_locks.available`, `_legacy_claim` or read_config would propagate out of `_stamp()` inside `close()` after the merge landed. That contradicts the promise in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE and phase-signoff.md that a failure here is 'a sentence ..., never a failed merge'. (b) mirror_stub writes the index (and stamp_merged now writes `status`) with no revalidation, against CLAUDE.md's 'Every command that mutates the manifest revalidates'. The stamp's lockless, unvalidated write was already there; the stub write and the status are new. -> Move the config read and lock acquire inside the try block and return the settle sentence on any exception. After writing the stub, revalidate the index and restore the prior bytes if it produces a finding.
R4 (low) plugins/audit/tests/test_close_phase.py s5-s8; plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py sv2-sv5: Two behaviours the phase promises have no test that could fail. (a) mirror_stub's handling of a lock held elsewhere, which should degrade to the settle sentence while the landing continues: s6/s7 run only with the lock free. (b) settle on the single-file layout: every sv case uses sharded=True, so the `_write_add(..., None, False)` single-file branch and its no-op 'nothing to settle' answer are never exercised. -> Add a case that holds the index lock from another identity, calls mirror_stub, and asserts ('', sentence naming settle) with the index bytes unchanged. Add a single-file settle case with a stale phase and bug, asserting stored values, one plan.settle row, and that a second run writes nothing.
R5 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_manifest_crossrefs.py _check_derived; plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/validate-manifest.py:129-139: Both new warnings put every stale record into one line. The docstring justifies this as not burying the verb's own output, but this repository's plan at HEAD carries 34 derived disagreements and 35 stale stubs. I measured that read-only with _mio.derived_disagreements / _mio.stale_stubs on docs/audit/audit-plan.json in the P69 worktree. So every write verb here now prints two multi-kilobyte WARNING lines until settle runs. I did not check whether _warning_groups.collapse elides them. -> Print the count, the first few ids and a --verbose pointer, as the other collapsed warnings do. Or confirm that collapse already shortens them, and say so in the docstring.
pre-existing 1 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/status/_doctor_completions.py has_receipt: `task.complete` still counts as a receipt for a task id alone. When the original close produced both rows (the main-checkout case), a task re-opened and then flipped back to done by hand stays hidden, so dc34's 'must still be found' holds only when no task.complete exists for that id. On the forgery question (P69.2): the new task.done receipt is strictly harder to forge than the old one. It needs a row for that taskId carrying the task's exact completedAt, and a hand edit that copies completedAt hides only a hand re-close after a re-open, which the id-only task.complete already hid. It hides no hand edit that was visible before. -> Make task.complete receipt a close only when no later re-open is recorded, or match on completedAt as task.done does.
pre-existing 2 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/panel/_panel_write.py:748-757: The panel's sweep builds its wanted/parents maps from recorded phase.branch only, not through manage-worktrees' branch_of, so it answers 'which branch is this phase's' differently from the CLI sweep. It is outside this diff and narrower rather than wrong. -> Share branch_of (or its answer) with the panel sweep, or document why the panel is deliberately narrower.
pre-existing 3 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/panel/_panel_state.py: _deps.layer_violations() reports 'runtime-loads render-report (layer 7) from layer 5'. Neither file is in the diff. close-phase (L7) importing _panel_write (L6) is downward and clean. -> Out of scope for P69; track separately if it is not already exempted.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: repro that FAILS on current code - re-opening a task in a signed-off parent-branch phase leaves a stored done over an open task and the next verb refuses the plan as invalid

outcome.technical: reopen verb under the index lock; _commit_trail clears fixedIn with its commit; mirror_stub guarded and revalidated; one warning per value kind; receipts match completedAt; branch_of shared via _branch.
outcome.descriptive: The phase review's findings are fixed: a reopen verb refuses to reopen work under a signed-off phase, a repair clears a stale fixedIn, and the stub mirror never fails a landing.
